Who buys it : coworking operators from single-location indies to multi-country brands. Their revenue is the conversion rate of the screens you'll design — CTAs, catalog, transitions, and checkout aren't decoration here; they're the product. How we work : small, agile, AI-heavy. On track to profitability this year. Headcount is deliberately small so each person owns real surface area — tight feedback loops, no bureaucracy, no committees. We measure shipped work — funnel lifts, partner themes shipped, UX issues triaged — not hours. No face-time theater. Co-located hybrid out of Workflow Thao Dien in HCMC for in-person speed. Wider team is async-first, written-first across US, Israel, Turkey, Philippines, and Vietnam. Weekly product/design sync with the CTO/cofounder — no layers between you and the people deciding what to build. Role Overview Product Engineer building the e-commerce platform behind the next generation of coworking spaces—SmartPricing, SmartMarketing, the booking engine operators embed on their sites, and the integrations that tie it all together. You work directly with the founders, with no layers between you and the people setting the roadmap. We also welcome final-year students looking for an internship. What engineering means here. The hard problem isn't writing code—AI writes plenty of it now. It's deciding what's worth building. Operators juggle hundreds of spaces, prices, members, bookings, and integrations across locations and time zones; customers comparing meeting rooms decide in seconds. Your job is to understand these humans—in the data—then ship software that moves their revenue. Empathy and data are the input; working product is the output. Polish comes last. On prioritization. Not all code has the same payoff. You'll look at a problem from several angles—funnel data, operator feedback, revenue, churn signals—and pick the work where your hours move the business most. A feature nobody uses is wasted hours; a 2% lift on the booking funnel is the company's quarter. Judgment over completeness. On decisions. Bigger calls go to the team before you build. Smaller calls—ship, watch the data, iterate. We're data-driven, not opinion-driven, and seniority doesn't win arguments—evidence does. You'll own the surfaces you touch, with support, and you expose your reasoning so we can calibrate together. On growth. You're early-career, and we hire for that on purpose. Expect code review, pairing, and direct coaching from founders and senior engineers. We can teach the stack, the patterns, and the product thinking. The one thing we can't give you is drive—that comes from you. What You'll Do Ship features end-to-end. Work with founders and operators to understand a need, then spec, build, and release it—with support along the way. Build and evolve our SmartPricing & SmartMarketing agents. Pricing rules, targeting logic, and performance monitoring. Make booking effortless. Seamless booking experiences with instant payment, embedded right in operators' websites. Wire up integrations. Sync data with coworking CRMs, inventory systems, and analytics tools—and prevent double bookings. Pull data, form an opinion, decide. Revenue, Mixpanel, GA4 / GTM funnel data, and operator feedback. Write so the team stays in sync. Clear specs and pull-request descriptions that keep an async, distributed team aligned across time zones. How You'll Work With AI Claude as peers, not novelties. You'll write and refine structured prompts, build new ones, and ship real changes through AI tools. Senior engineers coach you and set guardrails so you can move fast without first becoming a framework expert. Judgment, taste, and clear thinking are the bottleneck now—not syntax. We give you a budget for the best AI tools because we expect you to use them as leverage, not as a crutch. What Success Looks Like In Your First 6 Months You've shipped real features to production that operators and members actually use. You can navigate the codebase and pick up unfamiliar areas without much hand-holding. You ship changes through Claude with sound judgment about what to accept and what to rework. You back your decisions and pushback with data—and your written updates keep the async team moving without meetings. You're catching product, UX, and trade-off issues early, not just implementing tickets. What Makes You a Great Fit We prioritize these qualities top-down—technical skills can be learned quickly by sharp, curious people with low ego and a strong work ethic. Above all, here's what we look for: Drive and motivation. We can give you the tools, the environment, and hands-on coaching—but we can't give you the drive to succeed as a product engineer in the modern AI era. That has to come from you. Attention to detail and high standards. You're obsessed with quality—it's not about just getting the job done, it's about delivering the best work you can and raising the team's bar. You sweat the small things—edge cases, copy, data correctness—because details separate a working product from a trusted one. Clear written English. You read and write clear English (with the help with AI tools); in an async, globally distributed team, your writing is how you think, collaborate, and lead. High agency. You take initiative—ask questions when something's unclear, chase down answers, and push your work forward instead of waiting to be told the next step. You question everything. Everyone has a voice and is expected to push the envelope. There's no "the senior person knows better"—answers and pushback alike are grounded in data and critical thinking, regardless of title or age. Curiosity and fast learning. You pick up new domains, tools, and concepts quickly, especially around AI, pricing, and B2B SaaS. Product sense. You care about customers and business context, not just the tech stack, and you treat engineering as a way to drive revenue, bookings, and occupancy. You grasp basic microeconomics—incentives, opportunity cost, supply and demand—as a toolkit for trade-offs: simpler designs that still maximize value, arguments made in terms of impact rather than opinion, and an understanding of why the business prioritizes what it does. Don't have this thinking framework yet? If you bring the motivation, we'll coach you on it. Your Skills and Experience Must-have Vietnamese, based in Ho Chi Minh City . Hired on a Vietnamese employment contract. No visa sponsorship or relocation funding. Solid CS fundamentals. You understand how data is structured, how APIs work, and how to troubleshoot methodically—and you can name what you're doing and why. Comfortable with the basics that make a good teammate. Git, reading existing code, writing tests, and jumping into unfamiliar parts of a codebase. Some Ruby, TypeScript, or Python. You'll spend most of your time in Ruby and TypeScript. We don't expect all three—we expect you to learn fast. A project we can look at. At least one thing you built that works—side project, open source, internship, hackathon, or coursework—with a link and a clear story of how and why you built it. AI-native. You use Claude and Cursor daily and know where they shine and where they break down. Writing and reading English for async work. Speaking can be conversational—we coach. Agency. You spot things, fix things, ship things—you don't wait to be told. Self-taught software engineers are welcome. You don't have to study IT or computer majors to become a good software product builders. What matters is the drive, agency, attention to detail, willingness to ship, and how fast you learn. If you read this and thought "I could do that with some support," don't self-select out—apply. Why You'll Love Working Here This role suits future founders. Direct cofounder access, real ownership of decisions and outcomes, scope across an entire product surface, an inside look at how a small team turns AI into shipped product. If you aspire to build your own startup product one day, this is the seat that builds the muscles. Compensation & growth Salary: up to 26M VND/month GROSS. Calibrated on portfolio strength, interview sharpness, and demonstrated speed of learning, not years on a resume. Exceptional candidates can be discussed above this band. Comp reviews on request — if you've grown the role, raise it. Probation: 2 months at full salary. Passes on shipping consistently — no surprise gates. Stock options eligibility and a company laptop after probation. Bring your own laptop during probation. Tools Company-paid Claude Workspace & culture Covered desk at Workflow Thao Dien (HCMC). Hybrid at least 2 days/week in-person. Flexible hours. Vietnam time (ICT). Occasional pre-scheduled evening calls overseas, rare in practice. English-first, American startup culture: direct feedback, written-first, low-meeting. We measure shipped work, not hours. Benefits BHXH / BHYT / BHTN contributions per Vietnamese labor law. Vietnamese public holidays off (incl. Tết). Unlimited personal time off. Coordinate with the team based on urgency and your ownership. Hiring process Three real-time conversations with humans. No automated screening, no pre-recorded video tasks, no take-home gauntlet. Intro call — short conversation to get a sense of your English and how clearly you articulate your thinking. Team conversation — in person at Workflow Thao Dien. Walk us through your portfolio, talk shop, hang out, code together, grab lunch (we pay). Conversation with the CTO — remote (or in-person if on business trip). Product, technical fluency, working style.

job_description:
Top 3 Reasons To Join Us

The Job About the job Product Engineer AI-first engineering, uncompromising fundamentals. Accountable for the outcome, not the output. Full-time · On-site · Flexible working hours · Distributed, multi-timezone team · AI-first engineering · 3+ years experience The role is remote from your start date and becomes hybrid when our new office opens, expected around 20 December Job Summary We are hiring a Product Engineer - an engineer accountable for outcomes, not output . We do not measure engineers by tickets closed or lines shipped. We measure them by whether the thing they built actually solved the user's problem. That means you will be expected to question requirements before building them, own a feature from ambiguity through to production behaviour, and stay attached to it after release - watching the metrics, the logs, and the support tickets. You will work with Product Managers, designers, and business stakeholders based in different countries and timezones . Overlap hours are limited by design, so clear communication and the ability to move a decision forward asynchronously - without waiting for a meeting - matter as much as your engineering skill. This is a deeply technical role with an AI-first mindset . AI coding agents are the default way we build here - you will spend more of your day designing architecture, steering agents, and reviewing generated code than typing implementations by hand. We expect fluency with spec-driven development, reusable agent skills, and context engineering, not occasional autocomplete use. Which is exactly why fundamentals and best practices matter more, not less , so you will be held to a high bar on SOLID, Clean Architecture, design patterns, distributed system design, relational data modelling, and automation testing: these are working knowledge, not résumé keywords, and you should expect to defend your choices reasonably in code review and in the interview. You remain the author of record for everything that lands in main. "The agent wrote it" is never an acceptable explanation for a defect. Key Responsibilities Own the outcome. Take a business problem from vague to shipped to measured . Define what success looks like with your Product Manager, instrument for it, and act on what the data says - including rolling back or rewriting your own work when the numbers disagree with the plan. Find the problem, not just the solution. Interrogate requirements before implementing them. Surface the cheaper path, the edge case nobody scoped, and the feature that shouldn't be built. Say so early and in writing. Collaborate across borders and timezones. Partner directly with Product Managers, designers, QA, and business stakeholders distributed across multiple countries. Write decisions down, keep specs and PR descriptions self-explanatory, unblock people in other timezones, and run the occasional early or late call when the others need it. Architect and build services and APIs. Design RESTful (and where appropriate, event-driven or gRPC) services applying SOLID, Clean/Hexagonal Architecture, and design patterns deliberately - with a clear justification for the boundaries you draw. Design normalised, indexed, migration-safe relational schemas that hold up under real query load. Architecture is the part an agent cannot infer for you: you set the boundaries and the contracts, then let agents fill them in. Design for distribution. Make grounded calls on monolith vs. microservices. Build services that satisfy 12-factor principles - externalised config, stateless processes, disposability, dev/prod parity - and containerise them for Docker/Kubernetes deployment. Automate the safety net. Own automated testing for what you build: unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end where it earns its keep. Tests ship in the same PR as the code, not in a follow-up ticket. A bug fix without a reproducing test is not a fix. In an AI-first workflow the test suite is the specification - it is what makes agent-generated change safe to merge at speed. Work AI-first, and hold the line on quality. Drive delivery with coding agents, know your acceptance criteria first, let agents execute, then review hard. Build and maintain reusable agent skills, project instructions, and guardrails so the whole team gains leverage - not just your own throughput. Reject output that is merely plausible: over-abstracted layers, duplicated logic, silently swallowed errors, tests that assert nothing. Never merge code you cannot explain line by line. Run what you ship. Instrument services with structured logging, metrics, and tracing. Debug production incidents, write the postmortem, and close the loop with a fix that prevents recurrence. Raise the team's bar. Review peers' PRs substantively, document trade-offs and decisions, and mentor on fundamentals and on responsible AI-assisted workflows. Your Skills and Experience Job Requirements 3+ years building and operating production backend services - and you can walk through a system you designed, why you designed it that way, and what you'd change now. Deep, demonstrable command of software design fundamentals: OOP, SOLID, Clean Architecture, and design patterns. You will be asked to critique a design and explain what breaks at scale. This is the non-negotiable core of the role - in an AI-first team, fundamentals are the review capability that keeps agent velocity from becoming agent debt. Strong RESTful API design: resource modelling, versioning, idempotency, pagination, error contracts, authentication/authorisation. Strong relational database design (PostgreSQL/MySQL): normalisation and when to break it, indexing strategy, transactions and isolation levels, query analysis, safe schema migrations. Microservices and 12-factor apps: service boundaries, inter-service communication, failure isolation, configuration and secrets management - plus honest judgment on when a monolith is the correct answer. Automation testing discipline: you write tests first or alongside, understand the test pyramid, and use test doubles without mocking away the thing under test. You treat coverage as a floor for confidence, never as a number to satisfy - and you can tell a genuine regression test from an agent-generated one that asserts nothing. Containerisation: confident with Docker; working knowledge of Kubernetes (deployments, services, config/secrets, health probes, resource limits). An AI-first way of working, already in your hands: real production experience with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or equivalent - including spec/context engineering, agent skills or custom commands, and a disciplined self-review process before any PR. You should be able to describe a time an agent produced plausible-but-wrong code, how you caught it, and which fundamental (a design principle, a data-model rule, a failing test) let you catch it. Product mindset with real ownership instincts: comfortable with ambiguity, able to talk to non-engineers about trade-offs in their language, and biased toward shipping something small to learn rather than debating something large. Effective asynchronous, cross-cultural collaboration: professional written English, the discipline to document context for people who are asleep when you're working, and comfort operating with stakeholders in several countries and timezones. Working frontend ability - React, Next.js, or Vue - enough to build and ship a full user-facing slice yourself. Nice to Have Golang - our preferred backend language for new services. gRPC and HTTP/2 , including streaming and Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time and AI-streaming interfaces. ReactJS / NextJS at depth - SSR/RSC, routing, data fetching, performance. CI/CD pipeline ownership (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar) including automated quality and security gates. Infrastructure as Code - Terraform, Pulumi, or Helm. Service observability and SRE practice - OpenTelemetry, APM (Datadog / New Relic / Grafana stack), SLOs and error budgets, on-call and incident response. Message queues, background job processing, and event-driven architectures. SaaS products, media streaming (HLS/M3U8), or prior experience in a distributed international team. Why You'll Love Working Here What We Offer Office pantry, adjustable height desk, monitors, entertaining area, etc at office. Flexible working hours - we care when your work lands and how it performs, not when you were online. A genuinely international team - you'll work with product and business colleagues across multiple countries. Team building activities and company trips.

SAP & Enterprise Integration: Design, deploy, and monitor integration pipelines connecting internal applications to SAP S/4HANA / ECC and Microsoft 365 via OData (v2/v4), REST APIs, Azure Service Bus, Event Grid, and Logic Apps. Microsoft Azure certifications such as AZ-204 (Azure Developer Associate), AZ-104 (Azure Administrator), AZ-700 (Azure Network Engineer Associate), or AZ-400 (DevOps Engineer Expert). Frontend Experience: Solid commercial experience building and maintaining complex web frontends using React, client-side state management (e.g., Zustand, TanStack Query), and component libraries. This role plays a strategic and enterprise-wide leadership role in supporting VPBanks Securities’ ambition to become a leading securities and digital investment platform in Vietnam. The position is accountable for building a mature, resilient, scalable, and business-enabling information security capability that supports digital trading growth, cloud adoption, data-driven services, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience. Key Responsibilities Information Security Strategy and Governance Develop and execute the enterprise information security strategy aligned with VPBanks Securities’ business strategy, digital transformation roadmap, technology modernization, and risk appetite. Establish and maintain information security governance frameworks, policies, standards, procedures, and control requirements across the company. Define the information security target operating model, including people, process, technology, governance, metrics, and accountability. Provide strategic advice to senior management on cyber risk, information security priorities, regulatory expectations, and investment requirements. Drive a security-by-design culture across technology, product, operations, digital platforms, cloud, data, and third-party ecosystems. Enterprise Security Assurance Lead the overall security assurance program for trading platforms, core securities systems, customer portals, mobile applications, APIs, infrastructure, cloud platforms, data platforms, and critical business services. Oversee security reviews and risk assessments for new products, digital investment services, technology initiatives, outsourcing arrangements, vendor integrations, and major transformation programs. Ensure appropriate security controls are embedded throughout the system development lifecycle, change management process, cloud adoption journey, and production operations. Manage vulnerability management, penetration testing, red team exercises, secure code review, configuration review, and remediation governance. Establish measurable security control assurance and reporting mechanisms for executive-level visibility. Cloud and Digital Security Lead the security strategy and control framework for cloud adoption, including public cloud, private cloud, hybrid cloud, container platforms, DevSecOps, cloud-native applications, and cloud infrastructure. Define cloud security standards covering identity, network security, data protection, encryption, key management, monitoring, workload protection, configuration baseline, and compliance. Partner with technology, digital product, and trading platform teams to enable secure, scalable, and resilient digital services. Ensure that cloud and digital initiatives meet internal security requirements, regulatory obligations, and industry good practices. Lead the development and testing of cyber incident response plans, playbooks, escalation processes, and post-incident review practices. Support internal and external audits, regulatory inspections, and remediation programs related to information security. Maintain effective risk reporting, issue tracking, and remediation governance for executive committees. Strengthen identity and access management practices, including privileged access management, access governance, authentication, authorization, and zero trust principles. Ensure that customer data, trading data, employee data, partner data, and confidential business information are adequately protected across systems, channels, and third parties. Oversee third-party security risk assessments, contract security requirements, ongoing monitoring, and remediation follow-up. Ensure that external dependencies do not create unacceptable cyber, operational, regulatory, or reputational risks for the company. Leadership and Capability Building Lead, develop, and mentor the information security team, building strong capabilities across governance, architecture, assurance, operations, cloud security, application security, incident response, and risk management. Build a high-performance security culture with clear ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Design and deliver security awareness programs for employees, management, technology teams, and business units. Manage security budgets, resource planning, vendor performance, and capability development roadmaps. Strong understanding of securities technology architecture, online trading platforms, core securities systems, market connectivity, APIs, customer-facing digital channels, cloud platforms, data platforms, and enterprise infrastructure. Hands-on leadership experience across security operations, application security, cloud security, identity security, data protection, incident response, vulnerability management, and third-party security. Xây dựng mô hình dữ liệu (dimensional modeling, star schema, SCD) cho các nghiệp vụ đặc thù bán lẻ: fact giao dịch bán hàng theo dòng hóa đơn, snapshot tồn kho theo ngày/cửa hàng/SKU, đơn mua hàng và nhập kho, hủy hàng, hiệu quả chương trình khuyến mãi, khách hàng thành viên. Phát triển lớp transformation bằng SQL/dbt; tối ưu hiệu năng truy vấn và chi phí xử lý trên cloud data warehouse (BigQuery hoặc tương đương). 3. Phối hợp với đội System trong việc triển khai, vận hành hạ tầng cho các dịch vụ dữ liệu (container, cloud resource); đội System chịu trách nhiệm hạ tầng nền tảng.
